source_spans.locator: Journal of Neuroscience 19(5), pp.1736-1753 abstract: two stimuli within one receptive field induce competing neuronal responses.
Same abstract: directing task relevance to one member of the pair shifts the neuronal response toward the response produced by that stimulus alone.
Same abstract: with a single stimulus there is less competition to resolve and the selection manipulation has a more limited effect.

conditions: one or two visual stimuli presented within a neuron's receptive field
substrate: neurons in visual areas V2 and V4
task: behavioral selection of one visual stimulus while recording neuronal responses
temporal_scope: stimulus presentation followed by task-directed selection

nodes.description: two visual stimuli presented together within one receptive field
behavioral instruction that makes one member of the pair currently relevant
recorded response of a visual neuron
response pattern elicited when a candidate stimulus is presented alone

relations.description: adding a second stimulus changes the neuronal response in the direction associated with the additional stimulus
assigning behavioral relevance to one member of the pair shifts the response toward that member's single-stimulus reference
the task-dependent modulation is greater when competing stimuli are present than when a single stimulus is present
